slides.0.title: Oregon II: Willamette soils and styles
slides.0.subtitle: Jory, Willakenzie and Laurelwood
slides.1.title: Jory: the volcanic soil
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Origin
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Weathered from Columbia River Basalt flows that reached the valley about 15 to 10 million years ago, a red, iron-rich clay
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Where
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Typified by the Dundee Hills, and also found in parts of Eola-Amity Hills, Chehalem Mountains and McMinnville
slides.1.highlights.2.title: The usual style claim
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Richer red fruit, a silkier mid-palate and slightly fuller body
slides.1.content: Jory = basalt clay = Dundee Hills; the style descriptions are conventional wisdom, not regulation.
slides.2.title: Willakenzie: marine sedimentary rock
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Origin
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Siltstones, sandstones and mudstones laid down on the ocean floor about 60 to 40 million years ago and later uplifted; technically not volcanic soil
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Where
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Yamhill-Carlton and Ribbon Ridge, and parts of McMinnville, Chehalem Mountains and Eola-Amity Hills
slides.2.highlights.2.title: The usual style claim
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Darker fruit, firmer tannic structure and more floral and earthy aromatics
slides.2.content: Willakenzie = marine sedimentary = Yamhill-Carlton / Ribbon Ridge.
slides.3.title: Laurelwood: windblown loess
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Origin
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Silt-textured windblown loess from deposits about 15,000 to 13,000 years old (the Missoula Flood era), lying 1 to 3 metres over Columbia River Basalt
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Where
slides.3.highlights.1.content: The Tualatin Mountains and northern Chehalem Mountains; the Laurelwood District and Tualatin Hills AVAs (2020)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: The usual style claim
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Elegant red cherry and plum, fine-grained tannin and floral notes such as rose and violet
slides.3.content: The three soils map onto three groups of sub-AVAs and form the skeleton of Willamette terroir arguments.
What is the origin of Jory soil?
Red clay weathered from Columbia River Basalt.
Which two sub-AVAs mainly have Willakenzie?
A. Dundee Hills and Eola-Amity Hills
D. Van Duzer and Lower Long Tom
What kind of rock is Willakenzie?
Laid down on the sea floor and later uplifted.
